items.stem: An AI tool reports a favourable cost variance on a work package. The cost engineer notices the actuals were compared to an old baseline. What is the correct action?

options.text: Re-run the comparison against the current approved baseline before reporting
options.rationale: Correct: variance is only meaningful against the current approved baseline.

options.text: Report the favourable variance as-is because it looks good
options.rationale: A variance against the wrong baseline is misleading and must be corrected.

options.text: Delete the baseline to avoid confusion
options.rationale: The baseline is essential; the fix is using the correct, approved one.

options.text: Assume the AI chose the right baseline automatically
options.rationale: Baseline selection must be verified, not assumed.

items.explanation: Correct: variance is only meaningful against the current approved baseline.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices make an AI-assisted cost forecast trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Stating the assumptions the forecast depends on
options.rationale: Correct: explicit assumptions let others judge and challenge the forecast.

options.text: Recording who approved the forecast and when
options.rationale: Correct: a sign-off record maintains accountability for the forecast.

options.text: Presenting the forecast as a guaranteed out-turn
options.rationale: Forecasts are assumption-based estimates, not guarantees.

options.text: Hiding the input data from reviewers
options.rationale: Reviewers need the inputs to trust and check the forecast.

items.explanation: Correct: explicit assumptions let others judge and challenge the forecast.

items.stem: A controls report drafted by AI reads cleanly, but the underlying progress data was entered inconsistently by site teams. What risk does this create?

options.text: A polished report can present unreliable conclusions because the input data was poor
options.rationale: Correct: clean output does not fix dirty input; data quality must be checked first.

options.text: None, because a clean report guarantees clean data
options.rationale: Presentation quality says nothing about data quality.

options.text: The AI will automatically correct the bad data
options.rationale: AI does not inherently fix inconsistent source data.

options.text: The report cannot be wrong if it is well written
options.rationale: Well-written reports can still be wrong if the data is flawed.

items.explanation: Correct: clean output does not fix dirty input; data quality must be checked first.
